short: Constantine's victory over Maxentius outside Rome settled control of the Western Empire.
full:
On 28 October 312, Constantine's army met Maxentius's forces at the Milvian Bridge on the Tiber just north of Rome. Maxentius, holding the city, had chosen to fight in the open rather than endure a siege; when his line broke, the pontoon bridge his engineers had built collapsed under the retreat, and Maxentius drowned along with much of his army.

Constantine entered Rome the next day as unchallenged master of the West, and later accounts, including his own, attributed the victory to a vision or dream directing him to mark his soldiers' shields with a Christian symbol. The Praetorian Guard, which had backed Maxentius, was disbanded afterward and its camp demolished, ending an institution that had shaped imperial politics for over three centuries. The battle left Constantine positioned to become sole emperor within twelve years.
